name: sql_agent.py
summary: AI service agent that generates and interprets SQL queries using a local Ollama LLM within a Django backend.
purpose: To provide an intelligent interface for converting natural language or structured requests into executable SQL, reducing manual query writing and enabling AI-driven data access.
responsibilities: Generate SQL queries from natural language or structured inputs using an LLM
Interpret, explain, or refine existing SQL statements
Integrate with Django settings for LLM and database configuration
Format and engineer prompts specific to SQL generation tasks
Interface with higher-level AI query services to fulfill data requests
inputs: Natural language user queries or structured intent objects
Django configuration settings (LLM endpoint, model parameters)
Optional conversation history or prior query context
outputs: Natural language explanations of SQL logic
Validation feedback or error messages for invalid requests
Structured data objects for downstream service consumption
architecture_notes: Located in the backend AI service layer, this component encapsulates SQL-specific LLM interactions using LangChain's Ollama integration for local inference. It follows a specialized agent pattern, isolating prompt logic and SQL generation from general query orchestration handled by ai_query_service.py. Dependency on django.conf.settings indicates environment-driven configuration, though tight coupling to OllamaLLM suggests a concrete provider implementation rather than an abstracted LLM gateway.
improvements: Introduce an abstract LLM provider interface to decouple from Ollama and enable model swapping
Implement strict input validation and prompt injection guards before sending data to the LLM
Add an explicit schema ingestion mechanism rather than implicit context passing
Integrate a SQL validation or sandbox execution layer to verify generated queries before production use
Add caching for repeated or similar queries to reduce latency and LLM load
Include structured logging and tracing for LLM prompt/response cycles to improve observability
